title: Transactions, Concurrency, and Recovery

weeks.focus: Model and freeze invariants, boundaries, histories, and anomaly predictions
Build concurrent transactions and explicit correctness controls
evidence: Internals review and Week 30 learning log

weeks.focus: Break transactions, crash the store, and validate recovery
evidence: Failure matrix and Week 31 learning log
Evaluation, remediation, and Week 32 learning log

readiness_note: Ready on 2026-08-02 after semantic and evidence-safety review, nine transaction-lab tests across fourteen strict paired scenarios, six evaluator records with stable calibration bands, deterministic calibration checking, focused validation, full-course validation, and authoritative-resource verification.

outcomes.statement: Map business invariants to transaction boundaries, authoritative state, and enforceable constraints.
Derive isolation anomalies from histories, visibility rules, and serialization dependencies.
Implement and compare locking, optimistic validation, MVCC, deadlock handling, and bounded transaction retries.
Enforce atomic authoritative workflows with schema constraints and rebuildable derived state.
Explain and test WAL ordering, checkpoints, redo/undo, group commit, and durable acknowledgement.
Automate and validate backup, point-in-time recovery, integrity checks, and measured RTO/RPO while distinguishing replicas from backups.
Diagnose seven concurrency and recovery failures from immutable same-input evidence.
Defend a transaction and recovery strategy covering security, cost, operations, ownership, migration, rollback, and reversal evidence.

resources.title: Transaction Isolation
resources.purpose: Ground visibility, anomalies, and whole-transaction serialization retry in an operated DBMS.
resources.assignment: Read Sections 13.2.1-13.2.3; draw one admitted history per level and state which Northstar invariant it can violate.

resources.title: Explicit Locking
resources.purpose: Connect lock modes, wait behavior, and deadlock victim handling to application retry policy.
resources.assignment: Read Sections 13.3.2 and 13.3.4; build a wait-for graph and write a complete-transaction retry boundary.

resources.title: Database Systems Spring 2026 Schedule and Materials
resources.type: course videos with notes and slides
resources.purpose: Connect concurrency-control theory, 2PL, MVCC, logging, and recovery in one primary teaching sequence.
resources.assignment: Use only Lectures 17, 18, 20, 22, and 23; watch selected mechanism segments or use the linked notes, then annotate one schedule and one recovery trace.

resources.title: Write-Ahead Logging
resources.purpose: Derive WAL-before-data, redo, group commit, and PITR consequences from a concise implementation contract.
resources.assignment: Read the complete section; order log, data, flush, commit, and acknowledgement events and identify the unsafe permutation.

resources.title: Reliability and Storage Caches
resources.purpose: Bound durability claims across process, OS, controller, and device caches.
resources.assignment: Read Sections 28.1-28.2; list the flush assumptions the local lab cannot verify and the owner of each production check.

resources.title: Continuous Archiving and Point-in-Time Recovery
resources.purpose: Connect a base backup, complete WAL archive, recovery target, and restore time/storage cost.
resources.assignment: Read Sections 25.3.1, 25.3.2, and 25.3.5; draw the minimum recoverable set and calculate a bounded RPO and replay workload.

resources.title: Postmortem of database outage of January 31
resources.purpose: Show why successful backup jobs, replicas, runbooks, ownership, and tested restores are different claims.
resources.assignment: Read Broken recovery procedures through Root cause analysis; classify each failed control as prevention, detection, recovery, or ownership evidence.

resources.title: October 21 post-incident analysis
resources.purpose: Relate integrity-first degradation, large restore time, reconciliation, and backlog recovery to operating decisions.
resources.assignment: Read the recovery plan through Next steps; separate RTO, consistency, replay, backlog, and user-communication decisions.

WAL/data/flush/ack order, durable LSN, redo/undo, acknowledged effects, and uncertainty
result/audit authority, transaction boundary, constraint, crash point, and completeness
authoritative comparison, detection, rebuild, integrity probe, and excluded authoritative corruption
base/WAL identity, checksums, archive completeness, target, invariant probes, RTO, RPO, and traffic gate
